notes.title: Orders database (ORDB)
notes.summary: Primary PostgreSQL cluster holding customer orders and shipment bookings.
claims: ORDB runs PostgreSQL 15 on three nodes in the eu-west region.
ORDB is owned by the Data Platform team.
ORDB nightly snapshots are retained for 14 days.
Only the order-service account may write to ORDB in production.
Replica lag on ORDB read replicas triggers an alert at 30 seconds.

notes.title: Tracking events store (TRKDB)
notes.summary: Cassandra cluster that stores scan and GPS tracking events for every shipment.
claims: TRKDB is a nine-node Cassandra cluster owned by the Routing team.
TRKDB rows expire after a TTL of 400 days.
TRKDB ingests from the Kafka topic tracking.events.v2.
Queries on TRKDB must always include the shipment_id partition key; full scans are blocked.
TRKDB uses LOCAL_QUORUM for reads and writes.

notes.title: Reporting warehouse (REPWH)
notes.summary: Snowflake-based warehouse used for dashboards, finance reports and ad-hoc analysis.
claims: REPWH is hosted on Snowflake and administered by the Data Platform team.
REPWH is refreshed nightly by Airflow starting at 02:00 UTC.
REPWH keeps 18 months of shipment history; older data lives in the archive bucket.
Analysts get read-only roles on REPWH; write roles require a Data Platform ticket.
The default REPWH compute warehouse is size X-Small and auto-suspends after 60 seconds.

notes.title: Routewise transport management system
notes.summary: Internal TMS that plans delivery routes and dispatches loads to drivers.
claims: Routewise is currently on version 7.4 and is owned by the Routing team.
The Routewise dispatch cut-off for next-day routes is 17:30 local depot time.
Routewise gets drive-time matrices from the Pathly API.
Routewise re-plans open routes automatically every 15 minutes during the delivery window.
Planners can lock a route in Routewise to stop automatic re-planning.

notes.title: StockPilot warehouse management system
notes.summary: Warehouse management system running in all six distribution centres.
claims: StockPilot is deployed in six warehouses and owned by Warehouse Engineering.
StockPilot cycle counts are scheduled nightly for the A-class slotting zone.
Handheld scanners connect to StockPilot over the warehouse Wi-Fi VLAN 40.
StockPilot publishes inventory change events to Kafka topic wms.inventory.v3.
StockPilot upgrades are only allowed outside the Q4 peak season.

notes.title: Beacon customer portal
notes.summary: Web portal where customers book shipments, print labels and watch tracking.
claims: Beacon has about 4,200 active customer accounts.
Beacon is a React frontend backed by the public API gateway and is owned by Customer Integrations.
Customer logins on Beacon support SAML federation but not social login.
Beacon bulk shipment upload accepts CSV files up to 10 MB.
Beacon maintenance windows are Sundays 03:00 to 04:00 UTC.

notes.title: EDI gateway
notes.summary: Exchanges electronic documents such as shipment status and invoices with large customers and carriers.
claims: The EDI gateway supports X12 214, X12 210 and EDIFACT IFTMIN messages.
The legacy EDI v1 AS2 endpoint will be retired on 2027-06-30.
EDI v2 exposes a REST interface with JSON payloads and API keys.
About 38 customers still send orders through the EDI v1 endpoint.
The EDI gateway is owned by Customer Integrations.

notes.title: Public API gateway (Gatekeeper)
notes.summary: Front door for all customer-facing REST APIs, handling auth and throttling.
claims: Gatekeeper limits each API key to 600 requests per minute.
Gatekeeper authenticates partners with OAuth2 client credentials; tokens last 60 minutes.
Gatekeeper is operated by the SRE team.
Burst traffic above the limit receives HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.
Gatekeeper keeps request logs for 30 days.

notes.title: Event bus (Kafka bus-prod)
notes.summary: Central Kafka cluster that carries domain events between services.
claims: bus-prod has 12 brokers spread over three availability zones.
Default topic retention on bus-prod is 7 days.
Topic names follow the pattern domain.entity.vN, for example tracking.events.v2.
New topics need a Data Platform ticket and a named owning team.
Schemas are registered in the schema registry and must stay backward compatible.

notes.title: Airflow scheduler
notes.summary: Workflow scheduler that runs the nightly data pipelines and exports.
claims: Airflow runs version 2.9 and is operated by the Data Platform team.
At most 40 Airflow tasks run concurrently across all DAGs.
A failed Airflow DAG in the core-data group pages the Data Platform on-call after two retries.
DAG files live in the data-pipelines repository and deploy on merge to main.
Airflow connections hold no passwords; they reference secrets in the vault.

notes.title: Grafana and Prometheus monitoring
notes.summary: Metrics, dashboards and log search used by engineering and SRE.
claims: Prometheus keeps metrics for 45 days at full resolution.
Loki keeps application logs for 30 days.
Every production service must expose a /metrics endpoint and appear on a Grafana service dashboard.
Alert rules are stored in the sre-alerts repository.
The shared Grafana is reachable only over the VPN or the office network.

notes.title: Company VPN
notes.summary: WireGuard-based remote access to internal tools.
claims: The VPN is WireGuard-based and sessions expire after 12 hours.
Contractors from Brightdesk must use the VPN even for the staging environment.
VPN access requires an enrolled device and SSO MFA.
The VPN gateways are in Frankfurt and Dublin.
Split tunnelling is enabled; only internal CIDR ranges go through the VPN.

notes.title: Single sign-on (Authwise)
notes.summary: Identity provider for employees and contractors.
claims: Employee SSO is provided by the Authwise identity service.
MFA is mandatory for all SSO accounts; hardware keys are required for admins.
Passwords must be at least 14 characters.
Inactive SSO accounts are suspended after 60 days.
SSO group membership drives access to GitHub, Grafana and the VPN.

notes.title: CI/CD on GitHub Actions
notes.summary: Build and deployment pipelines for all services.
claims: CI runs on GitHub Actions with 20 self-hosted runners.
The build time target for service pipelines is 10 minutes.
Deployments to production are triggered from the deploy workflow on tagged commits.
Jenkins was decommissioned on 2026-02-28.
Pipeline secrets come from the vault via OIDC, never from repository secrets.

notes.title: Artifact registry
notes.summary: Stores container images and build artefacts.
claims: Untagged container images are deleted after 90 days.
All production images must be signed in CI before they are pushed.
The registry is hosted in the Cumulus eu-west region.
Images with critical vulnerabilities are blocked from production by an admission policy.
Release images are kept for 24 months.

notes.title: Secrets vault
notes.summary: Central store for credentials, keys and certificates.
claims: Database credentials in the vault rotate every 90 days.
Static secrets must have a named owner and a review date.
Developers have no read access to production secrets; services fetch them at runtime.
Break-glass access to the vault is logged and reviewed by Security the next business day.
The vault runs as a three-node cluster operated by SRE.

notes.title: Toggleboard feature flags
notes.summary: Service for runtime feature toggles.
claims: Every Toggleboard flag needs an owner and an expiry date at most 60 days away.
Expired flags are reported weekly to the owning team's Slack channel.
Flags that affect pricing need approval from Finance Systems before being enabled in production.
Toggleboard evaluates flags locally from a cache refreshed every 30 seconds.

notes.title: Haul driver app
notes.summary: Android app drivers use for stops, scans and proof of delivery.
claims: Haul runs on Android only; current release is 5.2.
Haul works offline for up to 8 hours and syncs when connectivity returns.
Proof of delivery in Haul requires a photo or a recipient signature.
Haul is built by the Mobile team.
Haul force-updates when the installed version is more than two releases behind.

notes.title: Label printing service
notes.summary: Generates shipping labels as ZPL for warehouse printers.
claims: Labels are generated as ZPL for 4x6 inch thermal stock.
The label service reaches carriers through the ShipLink aggregator.
Label generation latency p95 is under 400 milliseconds.
Reprints within 24 hours reuse the original tracking number.
The label service is owned by Warehouse Engineering.

notes.title: Address validation service
notes.summary: Cleans and geocodes delivery addresses at booking time.
claims: Addresses with a geocoding confidence below 0.82 are sent to manual review.
The service calls MapForge for geocoding and caches results for 30 days.
Corrections made by dispatchers are stored in the address corrections dataset.
The service is owned by the Routing team.
Postal code format checks cover 31 countries.

notes.title: Rate engine
notes.summary: Calculates freight quotes and surcharges.
claims: Rate quotes have a p95 latency target of 250 milliseconds.
Rate tables are reloaded every Monday at 05:00 UTC.
Fuel surcharge percentages are updated on the first of each month.
Contract rates for key accounts are stored separately from list prices.
The rate engine is owned by Finance Systems.

notes.title: Ledgerline invoicing
notes.summary: Produces customer invoices and posts to the general ledger.
claims: Ledgerline runs the monthly invoice run on the third business day.
Invoices are posted to the general ledger nightly at 23:30 UTC.
Credit notes above 5,000 EUR need Finance Systems sign-off.
Ledgerline is owned by Finance Systems.
Customers receive invoices by EDI or by email PDF.

notes.title: Customer sandbox environment
notes.summary: Test environment where customers certify their integrations.
claims: The sandbox mirrors the public API but returns synthetic shipments only.
Sandbox API keys start with sbx_ and cannot be used in production.
The sandbox is reset every Sunday at 01:00 UTC.
Customers must pass the certification checklist in the sandbox before getting production keys.

notes.title: Cold data archive
notes.summary: Object storage for shipment data older than 18 months.
claims: Archived shipment data is stored as Parquet files in the Cumulus archive bucket.
Restoring archived data takes up to 6 hours.
Archive objects are deleted after 7 years to meet retention rules.
Archive restore requests go through the Data Platform queue.

notes.title: MapForge
notes.summary: Vendor providing address geocoding.
claims: MapForge geocoding is contracted until 2027-03-31.
The MapForge contract allows 50 million geocoding calls per year.
MapForge replaced Geonexus as geocoder in June 2025.
The MapForge account manager is reached through the support portal, not by phone.
MapForge is called only by the address validation service.

notes.title: Pathly
notes.summary: Vendor of road network data and drive-time matrices used for routing.
claims: Pathly charges per matrix element requested.
The Pathly contract ends on 2026-12-31 and is under review.
Pathly provides the drive-time matrices that Routewise uses for planning.
Pathly traffic data covers Europe only.
The Pathly API key is stored in the vault under routing/pathly.

notes.title: Trackbox
notes.summary: Supplier of in-truck telematics hardware.
claims: About 2,300 Trackbox devices are installed in company and subcontractor trucks.
The current Trackbox firmware is 3.8.
Trackbox devices report GPS position every 30 seconds while moving.
Trackbox hardware has a three-year warranty.
Trackbox raw data lands in the driver telemetry dataset.

notes.title: Textline
notes.summary: Vendor sending delivery notification SMS messages.
claims: Textline sends delivery notification SMS to recipients under the sender ID FERNLOG.
Textline replaced Pingwave as SMS provider on 2026-05-01.
Textline provides sandbox keys that only deliver to whitelisted numbers.
Delivery receipts from Textline arrive through a webhook within 60 seconds.
Textline is billed per segment, not per message.

notes.title: Mailpost
notes.summary: Vendor for transactional email such as tracking updates and invoices.
claims: The Mailpost plan covers 2 million emails per month.
Emails from fernwick domains are signed with DKIM keys rotated yearly.
Mailpost bounces above 2 percent in a day trigger an alert to Customer Integrations.
Marketing email is not sent through Mailpost.

notes.title: Cumulus Cloud
notes.summary: Primary cloud infrastructure provider.
claims: Production runs in Cumulus eu-west; disaster recovery runs in eu-central.
The committed annual spend with Cumulus is 3.1 million EUR.
New Cumulus accounts can only be created by the SRE team.
Cumulus cost reports are reviewed monthly by Finance Systems.
The Cumulus enterprise agreement renews on 2027-09-01.

notes.title: Alertly
notes.summary: Paging and alert routing service used for on-call.
claims: The company holds 85 Alertly seats.
Alertly escalates unacknowledged pages after 10 minutes.
Alertly schedules mirror the on-call rotation defined in the SRE repository.
Alertly phone calls bypass Do Not Disturb on company phones.

notes.title: ShipLink
notes.summary: Aggregator giving a single API to many parcel and freight carriers.
claims: ShipLink connects the company to 40 carriers.
ShipLink charges 0.04 EUR per label created.
The label printing service creates all carrier labels via ShipLink.
ShipLink offers a test mode with fake tracking numbers.
The ShipLink contract renews each January.

notes.title: Tariffa
notes.summary: Customs broker integration and HS code classification.
claims: Tariffa handles customs declarations for EU and UK imports.
Tariffa classifies goods to 10-digit HS codes.
Tariffa filing cut-off is 14:00 CET on the day before arrival.
Disputed classifications are escalated to a Tariffa specialist within 2 business days.

notes.title: FuelNet
notes.summary: Fuel card provider for company trucks.
claims: FuelNet delivers a daily transaction file at 06:00 UTC.
About 410 FuelNet cards are active.
Cards are blocked automatically when a driver leaves.
Fuel transactions feed the cost allocation method.

notes.title: Redkite Security
notes.summary: External penetration testing firm.
claims: Redkite performs the annual penetration test every March.
The last Redkite report listed 4 high-severity findings, all fixed by 2026-06-30.
Redkite testers access staging only, never production.
Redkite reports are shared with the Security team and VP Engineering.

notes.title: Brightdesk contractors
notes.summary: Staffing agency supplying contract engineers and analysts.
claims: There are 22 Brightdesk contractors currently placed.
Placements are limited to 12 months.
Brightdesk contractors get SSO accounts that expire on the placement end date.
Brightdesk invoices are approved by the hiring manager and Procurement.

notes.title: Zephyr printers
notes.summary: Supplier of thermal label printers for the warehouses.
claims: Warehouses use the Zephyr ZP-420 thermal printer.
Zephyr printers carry a three-year warranty.
Replacement printheads are stocked at the Rotterdam warehouse.
Printer firmware updates are rolled out by Warehouse Engineering.

notes.title: ScanRight OCR
notes.summary: OCR service reading delivery notes and customs documents.
claims: ScanRight is billed 0.012 EUR per page.
ScanRight claims 99.1 percent character accuracy on printed documents.
Handwritten delivery notes are routed to manual review.
ScanRight is used by the exceptions workflow for damaged-goods claims.

notes.title: Helpdeskly
notes.summary: Ticketing tool for the IT helpdesk and access requests.
claims: Helpdeskly is the only supported channel for access requests.
Helpdeskly tickets are due for first response within 4 working hours.
Helpdeskly has 60 agent licences.
Helpdeskly integrates with SSO for requester identity.

notes.title: Data Platform team
notes.summary: Team running data stores, pipelines and the warehouse.
claims: Data Platform owns ORDB, REPWH, Airflow and the Kafka cluster.
The team is led by Marta Keller and has 9 engineers.
Data Platform office hours are Tuesdays and Thursdays 14:00 to 15:00 UTC.
Requests go through the data-platform Helpdeskly queue.
The team keeps a separate on-call rotation for core data pipelines.

notes.title: Routing team
notes.summary: Team that builds route planning and tracking systems.
claims: The Routing team owns Routewise, TRKDB and the address validation service.
Tomasz Wieczorek is the Routing tech lead.
The team has 12 engineers and 2 operations researchers.
Routing keeps a weekly planning review on Mondays at 10:00 UTC.

notes.title: Warehouse Engineering
notes.summary: Team that supports warehouse software and devices.
claims: Warehouse Engineering owns StockPilot, the label service and warehouse devices.
Lucas Ferreira leads the team of 8.
Site visits to each warehouse happen once per quarter.
The team supports warehouses in Rotterdam, Duisburg, Lyon, Milan, Gdansk and Barcelona.

notes.title: SRE team
notes.summary: Reliability engineers owning infrastructure, observability and incident response.
claims: SRE operates Gatekeeper, the vault, Grafana and the Cumulus accounts.
Dmitri Ocampo leads SRE; the team has 7 members.
SRE provides the incident commander roster.
SRE runs a game day every quarter.

notes.title: Security team
notes.summary: Team responsible for application and infrastructure security.
claims: The Security team is led by Nina Castellano and has 4 members.
Vendor security reviews are performed by Priya Nair.
Security reviews all new vendors that process customer data.
Vulnerability patching targets are 7 days for critical and 30 days for high severity.

notes.title: Customer Integrations
notes.summary: Team connecting customers and carriers to company systems.
claims: Customer Integrations owns Beacon and the EDI gateway.
Aiko Brandt manages the team of 10.
The team runs integration certification calls on Wednesdays.
Customer Integrations is on the escalation list for Mailpost bounces.

notes.title: Finance Systems
notes.summary: Team maintaining billing, rating and finance reporting.
claims: Finance Systems owns Ledgerline and the rate engine.
Hannah Osei is the senior analyst who signs off cost allocation.
The team closes each month's books on the fifth business day.
Finance Systems has 5 members.

notes.title: Mobile team
notes.summary: Builds the Haul driver app.
claims: The Mobile team builds Haul and has 6 engineers.
Omar Haddad leads the Mobile team.
Haul releases go out every second Wednesday via staged rollout.
The team keeps a physical device lab with 25 Android phones.

notes.title: QA team
notes.summary: Test engineering and release verification.
claims: The QA team is led by Ben Lindqvist and has 6 members.
QA owns the regression suite of 1,850 automated tests.
QA signs off every release train candidate before the Tuesday freeze.
QA maintains the anonymised test data set for staging.

notes.title: IT helpdesk
notes.summary: First-line IT support for employees.
claims: Jonas Aberg coordinates the IT helpdesk of 5 agents.
The helpdesk is staffed 07:00 to 18:00 CET on weekdays.
Laptops are issued from the Hamburg stock room.
Lost devices must be reported to the helpdesk within 2 hours.

notes.title: Marta Keller
notes.summary: Head of Data Platform.
claims: Marta Keller leads the Data Platform team.
Marta prefers asynchronous written proposals over meetings.
Marta approves new Kafka topics and warehouse role requests.
Marta is based in Hamburg.

notes.title: Dmitri Ocampo
notes.summary: SRE lead and incident commander coordinator.
claims: Dmitri Ocampo leads the SRE team.
Dmitri maintains the incident commander roster.
Dmitri is the escalation point for Cumulus account issues.
Dmitri works from the Dublin office.

notes.title: Priya Nair
notes.summary: Security engineer who runs vendor reviews.
claims: Priya Nair performs vendor security reviews.
Priya reviews every request for access to production customer data.
Priya hosts the monthly security clinic on the first Friday.
Priya has been in the Security team since 2024.

notes.title: Tomasz Wieczorek
notes.summary: Routing tech lead.
claims: Tomasz Wieczorek is the technical lead of the Routing team.
Tomasz wrote the original Routewise optimisation module.
Tomasz is the contact for Pathly technical questions.
Tomasz is based in Gdansk.

notes.title: Aiko Brandt
notes.summary: Manager of Customer Integrations.
claims: Aiko Brandt manages Customer Integrations.
Aiko signs off customer integration go-lives.
Aiko leads the EDI v1 sunset communication to customers.
Aiko is based in Lyon.

notes.title: Lucas Ferreira
notes.summary: Warehouse Engineering lead.
claims: Lucas Ferreira leads Warehouse Engineering.
Lucas decides which warehouse gets StockPilot upgrades first; Rotterdam is the pilot site.
Lucas is the contact for Zephyr printer warranty claims.
Lucas is based in Rotterdam.

notes.title: Hannah Osei
notes.summary: Senior analyst at Finance Systems.
claims: Hannah Osei signs off the monthly cost allocation.
Hannah approves flags that change pricing behaviour.
Hannah is the contact for Cumulus cost anomalies.
Hannah works Tuesday to Friday.

notes.title: Ben Lindqvist
notes.summary: QA lead.
claims: Ben Lindqvist leads QA.
Ben owns the release train go/no-go decision.
Ben runs the flaky-test review every Friday.
Ben prefers bug reports with a failing test attached.

notes.title: Sofia Reyes
notes.summary: VP Engineering.
claims: Sofia Reyes is the VP Engineering.
Sofia is the final approver for purchases above 50,000 EUR together with Procurement.
Sofia chairs the Change Advisory Board when escalations occur.
Sofia holds an open Q&A every last Thursday of the month.

notes.title: Omar Haddad
notes.summary: Mobile team lead.
claims: Omar Haddad leads the Mobile team.
Omar decides the Haul staged rollout percentages.
Omar is the contact for Android device lab bookings.
Omar is based in Barcelona.

notes.title: Elena Petrova
notes.summary: Procurement manager.
claims: Elena Petrova is the Procurement manager.
Elena negotiates all vendor renewals above 50,000 EUR.
Elena keeps the vendor contract calendar.
Elena prefers renewal notices at least 90 days in advance.

notes.title: Jonas Aberg
notes.summary: IT helpdesk coordinator.
claims: Jonas Aberg coordinates the IT helpdesk.
Jonas handles laptop refresh requests every 4 years.
Jonas can issue emergency loaner laptops the same day.
Jonas is based in Hamburg.

notes.title: Nina Castellano
notes.summary: Head of Security.
claims: Nina Castellano heads the Security team.
Nina is the named data protection contact for security incidents.
Nina approves exceptions to the password policy.
Nina reports quarterly to the board risk committee.

notes.title: Raj Subramanian
notes.summary: Data scientist owning the ETA model.
claims: Raj Subramanian owns the ETA prediction model.
Raj retrains the ETA model every Sunday night.
Raj documents model drift in the weekly data quality report.
Raj works remotely from Pune.

notes.title: Production deployment approval
notes.summary: Rules for who must approve a production deployment.
claims: Production deployments need two approvals since 2026-10-01: one from the owning team and one from SRE.
Approvals are recorded as pull request reviews on the deploy workflow.
Emergency fixes use the hotfix process instead and need the incident commander's approval.
Staging deployments need no approval.
Approvers may not approve their own changes.

notes.title: Change Advisory Board (CAB)
notes.summary: Review board for risky infrastructure and database changes.
claims: The CAB meets Tuesdays at 10:00 UTC.
CAB requests must be submitted by Monday 12:00 UTC.
CAB review is required for network changes, database major version upgrades and cloud account changes.
Routine application deployments do not go through the CAB.
Sofia Reyes chairs CAB escalations.

notes.title: On-call policy
notes.summary: How engineering on-call rotations work.
claims: Since 2026-07-01 on-call rotations are weekly with handover on Wednesdays at 09:00 UTC.
Primary on-call must acknowledge a page within 10 minutes.
On-call engineers receive 250 EUR per week and a day off in lieu after a night call-out.
A secondary on-call is required for services rated Sev1-critical.
Swaps must be arranged in Alertly at least 24 hours ahead.

notes.title: Incident response
notes.summary: Severity definitions and roles during production incidents.
claims: Sev1 means customers cannot book or track shipments; Sev2 is partial degradation; Sev3 is minor.
A Sev1 requires an incident commander from the SRE roster within 15 minutes.
Status page updates for Sev1 go out every 30 minutes.
Incident channels are named inc-YYYYMMDD-short-name.
A Sev1 or Sev2 requires a postmortem.

notes.title: Postmortem process
notes.summary: How incidents are reviewed afterwards.
claims: Postmortem documents are due within 5 business days of a Sev1 or Sev2.
Postmortems are blameless and name systems, not individuals.
Every postmortem action item needs an owner and a due date within 30 days.
Postmortems are stored in the engineering wiki under Incidents.
Dmitri Ocampo reviews postmortems for completeness.

notes.title: Vendor onboarding
notes.summary: Steps to approve and onboard a new third-party vendor.
claims: Vendors processing customer data need a Security review by Priya Nair before contract signature.
Vendors with expected spend above 50,000 EUR per year must go through Procurement.
A signed data processing agreement is mandatory for any EU personal data.
Vendor reviews take about 10 business days.
Approved vendors are added to the vendor register.

notes.title: Purchase approval
notes.summary: Who approves company spending.
claims: Managers approve purchases up to 5,000 EUR.
Directors approve purchases between 5,000 and 50,000 EUR.
Purchases above 50,000 EUR need the VP Engineering and Procurement.
Software subscriptions of any size must also be registered with the IT helpdesk.
Purchase orders are raised in the procurement tool before the invoice arrives.

notes.title: Access requests
notes.summary: How people get and keep access to systems.
claims: Access requests are filed in Helpdeskly and approved by the system owner.
Access to production customer data additionally needs Security approval.
Access is recertified every quarter by the system owner.
Temporary access expires after 7 days by default.

notes.title: Hotfix process
notes.summary: Fast path for urgent production fixes.
claims: Hotfixes bypass the release train but need an open incident ID.
The incident commander approves hotfix deployments.
Hotfix branches are cut from the latest release tag.
A hotfix must be merged back to main within 1 business day.

notes.title: Release train
notes.summary: Regular schedule for releasing core services.
claims: The release train departs every second Thursday.
Code freeze is Tuesday 18:00 UTC before departure.
QA must sign off the release candidate before the freeze.
No release trains run between 2026-11-23 and 2027-01-08 during peak season.

notes.title: Schema migrations
notes.summary: Rules for changing production database schemas.
claims: Schema changes use expand and contract in separate releases.
Migrations on ORDB need review by a Data Platform engineer.
Migrations that lock tables for more than 5 seconds are not allowed during business hours.
Every migration must have a tested rollback script.

notes.title: Staging data refresh
notes.summary: How staging gets its data.
claims: Staging is refreshed from anonymised production data on the first Sunday of each month.
Anonymisation replaces names, addresses and phone numbers with synthetic values.
Staging refresh is run by QA with Data Platform support.
Staging must not contain real customer data at any time.

notes.title: Personal data deletion requests
notes.summary: Handling of data subject deletion requests.
claims: Deletion requests must be completed within 30 days.
Nina Castellano is the contact for data subject requests.
Deletion covers ORDB, REPWH, TRKDB and the archive.
Backups are not edited; they age out after 14 days.

notes.title: Disaster recovery tests
notes.summary: Regular failover drills and recovery objectives.
claims: DR tests are run twice a year, in April and October.
The recovery time objective for ORDB is 4 hours.
The recovery point objective for ORDB is 15 minutes.
DR failover goes from Cumulus eu-west to eu-central.

notes.title: New hire setup
notes.summary: Standard setup steps for new employees.
claims: New hires get a laptop within 2 business days of their start date.
Access to GitHub and Slack is granted on day one via SSO groups.
New engineers shadow an on-call shift in their second month.
The helpdesk runs a 30-minute welcome session each Monday.

notes.title: Offboarding
notes.summary: Steps when someone leaves the company.
claims: Access is revoked within 1 hour after the last working day ends.
Laptops are returned within 5 business days.
FuelNet cards for departing drivers are blocked automatically.
Managers transfer ownership of services and vault secrets before the last day.

notes.title: Customer integration certification
notes.summary: Steps for certifying a customer integration before production use.
claims: Customers pass a 25-point checklist in the sandbox.
Certification typically takes 10 business days.
Aiko Brandt signs off the go-live.
Production keys are issued only after certification.

notes.title: Travel and expenses
notes.summary: Rules for business travel and claiming expenses.
claims: Expense claims must be submitted within 30 days.
Rail is required for trips under 500 km.
Hotels are capped at 160 EUR per night in major cities.
Mileage is reimbursed at 0.30 EUR per km.

notes.title: Move CI from Jenkins to GitHub Actions
notes.summary: Decision to retire Jenkins in favour of GitHub Actions.
claims: The decision to move to GitHub Actions was made on 2025-09-15.
Jenkins was switched off on 2026-02-28.
The main reason was maintenance cost of the Jenkins agents.
Self-hosted runners were kept for access to internal networks.

notes.title: Adopt Kafka as event bus
notes.summary: Why the company standardised on Kafka for events.
claims: Kafka was chosen in March 2024 over a managed queue service.
The goal was replayable tracking events for analytics.
Point-to-point HTTP callbacks between services are discouraged for new work.

notes.title: Choose Snowflake for reporting
notes.summary: Selection of Snowflake over BigQuery.
claims: Snowflake was chosen over BigQuery on 2024-11-12.
Deciding factors were separation of compute and cost predictability.
The team accepted slower ad-hoc cold starts in exchange.

notes.title: No Friday production deploys
notes.summary: Policy against deploying to production on Fridays.
claims: Production deployments on Fridays have been prohibited since 2026-03-02.
Hotfixes with an incident ID are exempt.
The rule followed three Friday-evening incidents in February 2026.

notes.title: Switch to weekly on-call rotation
notes.summary: Why on-call moved to shorter shifts.
claims: The weekly on-call rotation was approved on 2026-05-20 and started 2026-07-01.
Engineers had complained about two-week shifts causing fatigue.
The on-call allowance was raised at the same time.

notes.title: Replace Geonexus with MapForge
notes.summary: Switch of geocoding vendor.
claims: The geocoder switch was decided on 2025-04-08 and live in June 2025.
MapForge matched 4 percentage points more addresses in the trial.
Geonexus data was purged after 30 days.

notes.title: Replace Pingwave with Textline
notes.summary: Change of SMS provider.
claims: The SMS provider change was approved on 2026-03-12.
Pingwave delivery rates in Poland were below 90 percent.
Cut-over to Textline took place on 2026-05-01.

notes.title: Retire EDI v1
notes.summary: Decision to end the legacy EDI v1 endpoint.
claims: EDI v1 will be shut down on 2027-06-30.
Customers get migration help from Customer Integrations.
The date was postponed from 2026-12-31 because 38 customers had not migrated.

notes.title: Standardise on Python 3.12
notes.summary: Python version policy for services.
claims: All Python services must run Python 3.12 by 2027-01-31.
Python 3.9 images are blocked from the registry from 2026-12-01.
Services use uv for dependency management.

notes.title: Stay with multiple repositories
notes.summary: Decision not to move to a monorepo.
claims: The monorepo proposal was rejected on 2026-01-14.
Cross-repo changes use a shared dependency bot instead.
The decision will be reviewed in January 2028.

notes.title: Pull request size preference
notes.summary: Team preference for small reviewable changes.
claims: Pull requests should stay under 400 changed lines.
Large refactors are split into stacked pull requests.
Reviewers should respond within one working day.

notes.title: Meeting-free Wednesdays
notes.summary: Engineering keeps Wednesdays free of meetings.
claims: Engineering has meeting-free Wednesdays.
Integration certification calls are the only recurring exception.
Incident calls are exempt from the meeting-free rule.

notes.title: Architecture decision records
notes.summary: Convention to record architectural decisions as ADRs.
claims: Architectural decisions are written as ADRs in the docs repository.
ADRs use the template with Context, Decision and Consequences.
ADR numbers are sequential, starting at 0001.

notes.title: Use UTC for timestamps
notes.summary: Timestamps in systems and logs use UTC.
claims: All stored timestamps use UTC in ISO 8601 format.
Local times appear only in user-facing displays.
Meeting invites for cross-site events state the time in UTC.

notes.title: Service naming conventions
notes.summary: How services and repositories are named.
claims: Services are named in lowercase kebab-case, for example order-service.
Kafka topics use dots; Airflow DAG ids use underscores.
Environment suffixes are -stg and -prod.

notes.title: Incident communication style
notes.summary: How to write updates during incidents.
claims: Updates state impact, current action and the time of next update.
Avoid speculation about causes in customer-facing updates.
Internal updates go in the incident channel; customer updates go to the status page.

notes.title: Slack channel etiquette
notes.summary: Conventions for using Slack channels.
claims: Questions for teams go in the team channel, not direct messages.
Alerts go to channels prefixed alerts-.
Threads are expected for follow-ups.

notes.title: ETA prediction method
notes.summary: Gradient-boosted model predicting delivery arrival times.
claims: The ETA model is a gradient-boosted tree model owned by Raj Subramanian.
It is retrained every Sunday night on the last 12 weeks of data.
The target mean absolute error is under 18 minutes.
Features include traffic from Pathly, stop sequence and historical dwell time.

notes.title: Route optimisation approach
notes.summary: How Routewise solves vehicle routing problems.
claims: Routewise uses a heuristic vehicle routing solver with a 90-second time limit per depot.
Time windows are treated as hard constraints; driver breaks are soft.
Solutions are warm-started from the previous day's plan.
Solver improvements are benchmarked on 30 historical depot-days.

notes.title: Capacity forecasting
notes.summary: Forecasting shipment volumes for staffing and fleet.
claims: Volume is forecast 8 weeks ahead per depot using a seasonal model.
Peak season forecasts are adjusted by account managers for known promotions.
Forecast error is reported as WAPE; the target is under 12 percent.

notes.title: Warehouse slotting method
notes.summary: How products are assigned to pick locations.
claims: Items are ABC-classified by pick frequency every month.
A-class items occupy the golden zone between knee and shoulder height.
Slotting changes are executed on Sunday nights.

notes.title: Cost allocation method
notes.summary: How operating costs are allocated to shipments and customers.
claims: Costs are allocated per shipment using weight and distance drivers.
Fuel costs come from the FuelNet transaction files.
Hannah Osei signs off the allocation each month.
Warehouse costs are allocated by pallet-days.

notes.title: Tracking anomaly detection
notes.summary: Detecting shipments with missing or implausible scans.
claims: A shipment with no scan for 36 hours is flagged as possibly stuck.
Impossible speeds above 130 km/h between scans are flagged as GPS errors.
Flagged shipments appear in the delivery exceptions dataset.

notes.title: Daily shipments table
notes.summary: One row per shipment per day of status in REPWH.
claims: The table is shipments_daily in REPWH, loaded nightly.
Shipments cancelled before pickup are included with status CANCELLED.
The timestamp column event_ts is in UTC.
Rows before 2023-01-01 come from a legacy system and have no weight values.

notes.title: Carrier scorecards
notes.summary: Monthly on-time and damage metrics per carrier.
claims: Carrier scorecards are published on the fifth working day of the month.
On-time is measured against the promised delivery date, not the first attempt.
Carriers with fewer than 200 shipments in the month are excluded.

notes.title: Driver telemetry
notes.summary: Raw GPS and engine data from Trackbox devices.
claims: Telemetry records arrive about every 30 seconds per vehicle.
Telemetry is retained for 90 days in raw form.
Vehicle IDs in telemetry differ from fleet numbers; use the mapping table.

notes.title: Address corrections
notes.summary: Manual address corrections made by dispatchers.
claims: About 1,100 corrections are logged per week.
Corrections are keyed by normalised address hash.
The dataset is used to retrain the address matching rules.

notes.title: HS code reference
notes.summary: Mapping of goods categories to customs HS codes.
claims: The reference holds 10-digit HS codes for EU and UK.
It is refreshed from Tariffa every quarter.
About 3 percent of mappings are flagged as disputed.

notes.title: Warehouse inventory snapshots
notes.summary: Hourly stock levels per warehouse and SKU.
claims: Snapshots are taken every hour on the hour.
Negative stock quantities can appear for up to 2 hours after a scanner sync delay.
Snapshots older than 13 months are aggregated to daily.

notes.title: Delivery exceptions
notes.summary: Failed deliveries, damages and delays.
claims: Exceptions are categorised into 14 reason codes.
Reason code 9 means recipient unavailable.
Damage exceptions link to ScanRight-processed claim documents.

notes.title: Rate history
notes.summary: Historical list prices and surcharges.
claims: Rate history is versioned weekly on Mondays.
Key account contract rates are excluded for confidentiality.
Fuel surcharge values are stored as percentages with two decimals.

notes.title: Customer master data
notes.summary: Golden record of customer accounts.
claims: Customer master has about 6,800 accounts including inactive ones.
Customer IDs are 8 digits and never reused.
Duplicate accounts are merged monthly by Customer Integrations.

notes.title: Peak season operating rules
notes.summary: Special rules between late November and early January.
claims: Peak season runs from 2026-11-23 to 2027-01-08.
Non-essential production changes are frozen during peak season.
Extra on-call secondary coverage is added for Routewise and Gatekeeper.
StockPilot upgrades are not allowed during peak season.

notes.title: Customer SLA tiers
notes.summary: Gold, Silver and Bronze service levels.
claims: Gold customers get a 99.95 percent API availability commitment.
Silver customers get 99.9 percent and Bronze 99.5 percent.
Gold customers receive a named integration contact.

notes.title: Warehouse sites
notes.summary: List of the company's six distribution centres.
claims: Warehouses are in Rotterdam, Duisburg, Lyon, Milan, Gdansk and Barcelona.
Rotterdam is the largest site with 42,000 pallet positions.
Lyon operates only chilled goods.

notes.title: Carbon reporting
notes.summary: How CO2 figures are produced for customers.
claims: Emissions are calculated per shipment from distance and vehicle class.
Customers receive carbon reports quarterly.
The calculation follows the GLEC framework.

notes.title: Databases overview
notes.summary: Hub comparing ORDB, TRKDB and REPWH.
claims: ORDB is PostgreSQL for orders, TRKDB is Cassandra for tracking, REPWH is Snowflake for analytics.
Data Platform owns ORDB and REPWH; Routing owns TRKDB.
Use REPWH for reporting queries, never ORDB.
Retention differs: ORDB 14-day snapshots, TRKDB 400-day TTL, REPWH 18 months.

notes.title: Vendor landscape
notes.summary: Hub listing vendors by function.
claims: Geocoding is MapForge; road matrices are Pathly; carrier labels go through ShipLink.
Messaging uses Textline for SMS and Mailpost for email.
Infrastructure and paging come from Cumulus Cloud and Alertly.
Staffing comes from Brightdesk and penetration testing from Redkite.

notes.title: On-call and incidents hub
notes.summary: Hub linking on-call, incident response and postmortems.
claims: On-call is weekly; incidents follow Sev1 to Sev3 definitions.
Alertly pages the on-call; SRE supplies incident commanders.
Postmortems are due within 5 business days.

notes.title: Deployment and release hub
notes.summary: Hub covering how code reaches production.
claims: Routine releases follow the release train; urgent fixes use the hotfix process.
Production deployments need two approvals; infrastructure changes also need CAB.
No deployments on Fridays or during peak season freeze.
CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions.

notes.title: Security overview
notes.summary: Hub for security policies and owners.
claims: Security is led by Nina Castellano; vendor reviews by Priya Nair.
SSO with mandatory MFA fronts all internal tools.
Secrets live in the vault and rotate every 90 days.
Pen tests are run yearly by Redkite.

notes.title: Data quality caveats
notes.summary: Hub of known data caveats.
claims: shipments_daily has no weights before 2023-01-01.
Inventory snapshots can show negative stock after sync delays.
Telemetry vehicle IDs do not equal fleet numbers.
Carrier scorecards exclude carriers with under 200 shipments a month.

notes.title: Warehouse operations hub
notes.summary: Hub for warehouse systems and methods.
claims: StockPilot, the label service and Zephyr printers are owned by Warehouse Engineering.
Slotting is ABC-based and applied on Sunday nights.
Six sites run StockPilot; Rotterdam is the pilot.

notes.title: Routing and tracking hub
notes.summary: Hub for planning and visibility topics.
claims: Routewise plans with Pathly matrices and a heuristic solver.
TRKDB stores tracking events; the ETA model predicts arrivals.
Address validation uses MapForge geocoding.

notes.title: Customer integration hub
notes.summary: Hub for how customers connect.
claims: Customers connect via Beacon, REST through Gatekeeper, or EDI.
Certification happens in the sandbox before production keys are issued.
EDI v1 retires on 2027-06-30.

notes.title: Finance systems hub
notes.summary: Hub for billing, rating and cost topics.
claims: Finance Systems owns Ledgerline and the rate engine.
Monthly cost allocation is signed off by Hannah Osei.
Purchases follow the purchase approval tiers.

notes.title: Joining the company hub
notes.summary: Hub for new joiners.
claims: Laptop within 2 business days; access through SSO groups.
New engineers shadow on-call in month two.
Questions go to team Slack channels and Helpdeskly.

notes.title: Staging versus production rules
notes.summary: Hub contrasting rules in staging and production.
claims: Staging deployments need no approval; production deployments need two.
Staging never sends real SMS or email; sandbox keys only.
Staging holds anonymised data refreshed monthly; production holds real data.
Contractors need the VPN for staging; production access also needs Security approval.
Redkite pen tests target staging only.

notes.title: Monitoring and alerting hub
notes.summary: Hub for metrics, logs and alert routing.
claims: Prometheus keeps 45 days, Loki 30 days.
Alerts are defined in the sre-alerts repository and route through Alertly.
Gatekeeper logs are kept 30 days.

notes.title: Who to ask
notes.summary: Hub mapping topics to the right person.
claims: Data and warehouse: Marta Keller; infrastructure: Dmitri Ocampo.
Vendors: Priya Nair for security, Elena Petrova for contracts.
Customer integrations: Aiko Brandt; mobile: Omar Haddad.

notes.title: Key engineering decisions
notes.summary: Hub listing major decisions with dates.
claims: Kafka chosen 2024; Snowflake chosen 2024-11-12.
Jenkins retired 2026-02-28; Friday deploys banned 2026-03-02.
Weekly on-call from 2026-07-01; Textline live 2026-05-01.

notes.title: Dataset catalogue
notes.summary: Hub listing key datasets.
claims: Core tables live in REPWH, such as shipments_daily and carrier_scores.
Raw telemetry is kept 90 days.
Address corrections and delivery exceptions feed quality improvement.

notes.title: Driver mobile hub
notes.summary: Hub for the driver app and devices.
claims: Haul runs on Android, built by the Mobile team.
Offline mode lasts 8 hours.
Releases go out every second Wednesday.

notes.title: Compliance and retention
notes.summary: Hub for retention and privacy obligations.
claims: Deletion requests are done within 30 days.
Archive objects are kept 7 years.
DR test twice a year with 4 hour RTO for ORDB.

notes.title: Carrier network hub
notes.summary: Hub for carrier connectivity and scoring.
claims: ShipLink connects 40 carriers.
Carrier scorecards come out on the fifth working day.
Labels are ZPL and created via ShipLink.

notes.title: CI/CD and tooling hub
notes.summary: Hub for build tooling and registries.
claims: GitHub Actions replaced Jenkins.
Images are signed and stored in the registry.
Python 3.12 is the standard with uv.

notes.title: Glossary of acronyms
notes.summary: Hub defining internal acronyms.
claims: ORDB, TRKDB and REPWH are the three core databases.
CAB is the Change Advisory Board; TMS is Routewise; WMS is StockPilot.
POD means proof of delivery; RTO and RPO are recovery objectives.

notes.title: Code review rules
notes.summary: Minimum requirements for reviewing changes before merge.
claims: Every pull request needs one approving review from a code owner.
Security-sensitive paths such as auth and vault clients need a second review from the Security team.
Reviews must be completed within one working day.
Merging to main is blocked while CI is red.

notes.title: Fleet register
notes.summary: Register of company and subcontractor vehicles.
claims: The register lists about 1,650 vehicles, including subcontractor trucks.
Each vehicle has a fleet number and a separate Trackbox device ID.
Subcontractor vehicles are updated monthly, company vehicles weekly.

history.claim: Gatekeeper limited each API key to 300 requests per minute.
Production deployments needed only one approval from the owning team.
On-call rotations lasted two weeks with handover on Mondays at 08:00 UTC.
On-call engineers received 150 EUR per week.
ORDB nightly snapshots were retained for 7 days.
REPWH was refreshed nightly starting at 04:00 UTC.
Delivery SMS messages were sent through Pingwave with sender ID FERNLOG until 2026-04-30.
CI ran on Jenkins with 8 build agents.
Deletion requests had to be completed within 45 days.
Haul worked offline for only 4 hours.
Database credentials in the vault rotated every 180 days.
Access was recertified annually.
The MapForge contract allowed 30 million geocoding calls per year.
The EDI v1 AS2 endpoint was due to be retired on 2026-12-31.
The release train departed every week on Thursdays.
Toggleboard flags could have an expiry up to 90 days away.
The recovery time objective for ORDB was 8 hours.
Brightdesk placements were limited to 6 months.
TRKDB rows expired after a TTL of 180 days.
Managers could approve purchases only up to 2,000 EUR.
Addresses with geocoding confidence below 0.75 were sent to manual review.
